title: Structure of integral constructible complexes
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\pi_E$. Thus $X$ is Noetherian, and we work with the coefficient sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,X}$ and the categories $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ and $\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$ in the integral-model setting of [sk-lem-integral-models] and with constructibility as in [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

1. $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ is a triangulated subcategory of
   $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$, its objects are bounded, and it is
   stable under the standard truncations. The category $\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$
   of constructible $\mathcal O_{E,X}$-modules consists of the objects of
   $\Dbc(X,\mathcal O_E)$ concentrated in degree $0$, and is an essentially
   small abelian subcategory of $\Mod(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)$
   closed under extensions.
2. For $C\in\Cons(X,\mathcal O_E)$ there is a finite stratification of $X$
   such that on each stratum $C$ is pro-étale locally the completion of a
   finitely generated $\mathcal O_E$-module, possibly with torsion.
3. On each such stratum, $C$ is dualizable in the derived category (it admits a dual with evaluation and coevaluation satisfying the two triangle
   identities), of Tor amplitude in $[-1,0]$, and its dual has Tor amplitude in $[0,1]$.

proof.text: The opening hypotheses are the finite-type integral-model setting: [sk-lem-integral-models] supplies the separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$, its Noetherianity, and the finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with coefficient ring $\mathcal O_E$. Apply [det-lem-int-integral-heart-triangulated](1) to this integral coefficient category. Its statement gives all three assertions about $\Dbc$: it is a triangulated subcategory of the indicated ambient derived category, every object is bounded, and both standard truncations preserve it. These are the first assertions of (1).

By [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $\Dbc$ is defined by bounded constructible cohomology and $\Cons$ is the full subcategory of constructible modules. For a module $C$ placed in degree $0$, its only possibly nonzero cohomology is $H^0=C$. Thus it belongs to $\Dbc$ exactly when $C\in\Cons$. Apply [det-lem-int-integral-heart-triangulated](2) to this very full subcategory: kernels and cokernels computed in the ambient module category belong to it, it is closed under extensions, and it is essentially small. This proves the remaining assertions of (1), including the ambient, rather than merely abstract, abelian-subcategory assertion.

source.place: paragraph 4, heart and essential smallness; detailed triangulated statement (2)

proof.text: Let $C\in\Cons$. Regard $C$ as a degree-zero object of $\Dbc$, as established in step 2. Apply [det-lem-int-integral-heart-local-model](1),(2) to $K=C$ and take $q=0$. The finite stratification supplied in (1) is the same stratification on which (2) identifies $H^0(K)=C$ locally with the completion of the finitely generated module $H^0(M^\bullet)$. No torsion-freeness is asserted or needed. This is (2).

source.place: paragraphs 2 and 3, local models and cohomology

proof.text: Fix any stratum $S$ of the stratification in step 3. The sheaf $C$ is constructible and on $S$ has exactly the finite-module local model required by [det-lem-int-integral-heart-dualizable]. Its statement therefore supplies the derived dual $R\mathcal{H}om(C|_S,\mathcal O_{E,S})$, dualizability on all of $S$, Tor amplitude $[-1,0]$ for $C|_S$, and Tor amplitude $[0,1]$ for that dual. This proves (3), without replacing the derived dual by the underived module dual. In particular the cited statement explicitly includes the torsion example $\mathcal O_E/\pi_E$ with dual $\mathcal O_E/\pi_E[-1]$.

source.place: paragraphs 4 and 5, local dual and torsion example
